A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StableMaterials and provide readable methods, equations, experiments, references, and trailing qualitative-results pages. Figures and tables can be matched reliably despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V3 reports original material-generation examples, quantitative comparisons, reconstruction ablations, and inference-time measurements in Sections 4.2–4.4 and Figures 4–12.

after.justification: V4 retains those original experiments and adds a study of expert preferences and material-quality ratings in Section 4.3.

M1.justification: The VAE, semi-supervised losses, discriminator, feature rolling, consistency distillation, and refinement procedure are retained. The added statement that only ground-truth material latents count as real clarifies the existing discriminator description without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: V4 adds an evaluation population of 20 domain experts. The material datasets, SDXL texture data, image/text generation tasks, and in-domain/out-of-domain material coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Figures 6–7 and Table 1 retain their comparator sets: MatFuse, MatGen, Material Palette for image comparison, and Substance 3D Sampler replacing Material Palette for text comparison. The new user study uses the existing text-comparison baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 introduces a substantially different evaluation protocol: 20 experts assess ten prompts, select preferred outputs, and rate four methods on 1–5 scales for prompt fidelity, realism, and material consistency. Existing training and automated-evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: The VAE architecture, semi-supervised training, refinement, and patching ablations remain unchanged in Table 2 and Figures 8–9. Figure 10 retains the same failure cases; the user study is a comparative evaluation rather than a new ablation.

E5.justification: V4 first introduces formal statistical analysis: one-way ANOVA (F = 60.5, p < 0.05), a preference-count chi-square test (120.44, p < 0.001), and rating–preference correlation (R = 0.99). These concern the new study; existing benchmark tables gain no repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V4 adds a new body of human-quality results: preference counts are 105 for StableMaterials, 66 for Sampler, 25 for MatGen, and 4 for MatFuse; corresponding average ratings are 3.50, 2.71, 2.28, and 1.85. Tables 1–2, inference measurements, and existing qualitative examples remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, losses, and consistency-model description are retained. Splitting the supervised loss across separately numbered lines and renumbering the adversarial loss are typesetting changes, not mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims concerning semi-supervised material generation, distillation, feature rolling, and fast high-resolution synthesis. The user study supplies additional support without redefining those claims.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and limitations concerning spatial relations, complex patterns, incorrect reflectance, and unannotated-data coverage are retained. The new study reports preferences and statistical findings without adding a substantive explanation of mechanisms or applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: V3 promises future availability; v4 states public availability and supplies a project URL. Section 3.3 additionally specifies that only ground-truth material latents are discriminator real samples. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, training budgets, and inference details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to material-generation, diffusion, and distillation research are retained. Author–year citations become numbered references, with bibliographic formatting changes but no substantive literature expansion.

P1.justification: V4 condenses contribution and method passages, converts the enumerated loss overview into prose, and changes numbered ablation subsubsections into unnumbered headings. The affiliation changes from Independent Researcher to Adobe Research; the main narrative order remains intact.

P2.justification: The entire document adopts different typography, title/author formatting, headers, and caption placement. Figures 4–7 are distributed across two pages instead of one, and tables and ablation figures are rearranged. Figures 11–12 retain their result grids within the new layout.

improvement.justification: The expert study adds useful perceptual evidence beyond v3's examples and CLIP metrics. The discriminator clarification and project access information also improve documentation. However, the study does not explain rating aggregation or how repeated judgments across participants and prompts enter the statistical analysis, limiting the strength of the added validation.
